metadata.title: The Shadow Brokers (2016-17): when leaked NSA cyber-weapons became global ransomware
metadata.frame: An entity calling itself 'The Shadow Brokers' auctioned then dumped a cache of offensive tools attributed to the NSA-linked Equation Group. The April-2017 dump included EternalBlue (an SMBv1 exploit), which within weeks powered WannaCry (attributed to North Korea) and NotPetya (attributed to Russia) - the canonical case of state cyber-weapons leaking and boomeranging into worldwide damage.
metadata.grade: The leak, EternalBlue, MS17-010, and the WannaCry/NotPetya outbreaks = FACT. Attribution of WannaCry->DPRK/Lazarus and NotPetya->Russia/GRU = official government attributions (US/UK et al.) - strong but state-asserted. The identity of 'The Shadow Brokers' themselves is UNRESOLVED (Russia widely suspected; not proven).
metadata.honest_limits: Attribution of the outbreaks is by governments and vendors (high-confidence, still assertions). Who The Shadow Brokers are - and how they obtained the tools (insider? hack?) - remains publicly unresolved; this block does not assert it. NotPetya damage (~$10B) is an estimate.
metadata.method: Microsoft MS17-010 (Mar 2017); US-CERT; US/UK government attributions (WannaCry->DPRK 2017; NotPetya->Russia 2018); vendor analyses.

edges.notes: From Aug-2016 the Shadow Brokers auctioned/teased, then (Apr-2017) dumped, a cache of offensive tools attributed to the Equation Group (NSA's Tailored Access Operations) - exploits, implants, and the FuzzBunch framework (fact).

The leaked tools are attributed to the NSA (via Equation Group / TAO); the identity of the Shadow Brokers themselves is UNRESOLVED (Russian state widely suspected; an insider theory also floated - not proven). Present as open (fact of tool-attribution; actor-attribution open).

The Apr-14-2017 'Lost in Translation' dump released EternalBlue (SMBv1 remote code execution) + DoublePulsar implant. Microsoft had quietly patched it (MS17-010, Mar-14-2017) after a reported tip - one month before the public dump (fact).
EternalBlue exploited Windows SMBv1; unpatched/legacy systems (incl. end-of-life XP) remained exposed - the long tail of patch lag is what made the follow-on worms so damaging (fact).
May-12-2017: WannaCry ransomware used EternalBlue to self-propagate to ~200k+ machines in 150+ countries (incl. UK NHS); halted by a researcher's kill-switch domain (fact).
The US, UK and allies attributed WannaCry to North Korea (Lazarus Group), Dec-2017 - official government attribution (strong, state-asserted).
Code/infra overlaps tied WannaCry to Lazarus (the DPRK cluster also behind major crypto thefts) - linking the ransomware to the existing Lazarus node (fact per attribution).

Jun-27-2017: NotPetya (wiper masquerading as ransomware) used EternalBlue + Mimikatz, seeded via a compromised Ukrainian tax-software update (M.E.Doc); est. ~$10B global damage (Maersk, Merck, FedEx/TNT) (fact; damage estimate).
The US, UK and allies attributed NotPetya to the Russian military (GRU), Feb-2018 - official government attribution (strong, state-asserted).

The defining lesson: offensive cyber tools stockpiled by states leak and boomerang; EternalBlue kept powering intrusions for years. The core argument against 'nobody but us' vulnerability hoarding + for coordinated disclosure (fact of recurrence).
